description: Air China PhoenixMiles mileage (in kilometres) and qualifying segments for Air China flights. Mileage = distance in km (the great-circle miles x 1.609344; Air China uses the IATA distance) x booking-class %, at least 1,000 km in First, 800 in Business and 500 in Premium Economy and Economy; where Air China prints two rates, the first is a flight within Mainland China (both airports CN) and the second an international or regional flight (Hong Kong, Macao and Taiwan count as regional). Classes O, I, X and N earn nothing. The 25/30/50% elite bonus is a note only. Qualifying kilometres for the flight are not calculated (Air China does not say they equal the mileage earned), so the flight is not added to the progress. Cards need Silver 40,000, Gold 80,000 or Platinum 160,000 qualifying km, or 25 / 40 / 90 qualifying segments, in 12 months; qk and qs are the member's own totals so far, used only for the progress. Give segs: one entry per one-way flight, in order, with its great-circle miles (calculate_flight_distance gives them) and the ISO country codes of its two airports. Takes no price. Uses cwsi.net's calculator and the airline's published rules. Unofficial.

cls.description: Booking class. F = F (First 300%); A = A (First 200% / 250%); J = J (Business 300% / 250%); C = C (Business 200%); D = D (Business 150%); Z = Z (Business 125%); R = R (Business 110% / 125%); G = G (Premium Economy 110%); E = E (Premium Economy 90%); Y = Y (Economy 110%); B = B (Economy 100% / 110%); M = M (Economy 100%); U = U (Economy 100% / 75%); H = H (Economy 75%); Q = Q (Economy 75%); V = V (Economy 75%); W = W (Economy 50%); S = S (Economy 50%); T = T (Economy 50%); L = L (Economy 25%); K = K (Economy 25%); P = P (Economy 25%); O = O (earns nothing); I = I (earns nothing); X = X (earns nothing); N = N (earns nothing). The letter on your Air China ticket. A class with two percentages pays the first on flights within Mainland China and the second on international and regional flights.

creditClass.description: The booking class letter for creditTo, when it differs from the class question. Ignored without creditTo.

creditFlights.description: The flights for creditTo: one entry per one-way flight, in order, with its great-circle miles (calculate_flight_distance gives them) and optionally from/to airport codes. Defaults to segs when they carry miles.

from.description: The departure airport's code; labels the breakdown.

miles.description: Great-circle distance of this flight in miles.

to.description: The arrival airport's code; labels the breakdown.

creditStatus.description: Your status in the creditTo program, by its name as listed under creditTo. Defaults to the base level. Ignored without creditTo.

creditTo.description: Credit the flights to a partner program instead of Air China's own: united = United MileagePlus (creditStatus one of: General member, Premier Silver, Premier Gold, Premier Platinum, Premier 1K); aeroplan = Aeroplan (creditStatus one of: Aeroplan Member, 25K, 35K, 50K, 75K, Super Elite). Earns by each flight's distance and the booking class at the program's published partner rates; leave creditTo out for the airline's own program. The booking class is cls (or creditClass). The flights are segs (their miles), or creditFlights.

qk.description: Qualifying kilometres you have in the last 12 months (optional). Used only for the progress toward the next card; the flight is not added.

qs.description: Qualifying segments you have in the last 12 months (optional). Segments can be fractions, for example 1.1 in Y. Used only for the progress toward the next card; the flight is not added.

segs.description: The flights, one way and in order, one entry per flight (1 to 8): fromCountry and toCountry, the ISO 3166 two-letter country codes of its two airports; miles, its great-circle distance in miles (1 to 12,500); optional from and to, the IATA codes of its two airports, which label the breakdown; some airlines also use them (Vladivostok, VVO, on JAL and ANA; the Madrid-Barcelona Air Shuttle, MAD-BCN, on Iberia; the long-haul tables named by city on SAS).

from.description: The departure airport's IATA code, e.g. SYD. Labels the breakdown; JAL and ANA use it to spot Vladivostok (VVO), Qantas to pick its route tables, Iberia to spot the Madrid-Barcelona Air Shuttle (MAD, BCN), and SAS to pick its long-haul tables (named by city).

fromCountry.description: ISO 3166 two-letter country code of the departure airport, e.g. DE.

miles.description: Great-circle distance of this flight in miles.

to.description: The arrival airport's IATA code, e.g. SYD. Labels the breakdown; JAL and ANA use it to spot Vladivostok (VVO), Qantas to pick its route tables, Iberia to spot the Madrid-Barcelona Air Shuttle (MAD, BCN), and SAS to pick its long-haul tables (named by city).

toCountry.description: ISO 3166 two-letter country code of the arrival airport, e.g. DE.

status.description: Your PhoenixMiles card. NO = Not an elite member; SI = Silver (+25%); GO = Gold (+30%); PL = Platinum (+50%). Elite members earn extra mileage on Air China group flights. It is shown as a note, not added, because Air China does not say what it is a percentage of.

trip.description: Trip. ow = One way; rt = Round trip. Round trip counts the same flights back the other way.
